introduction: A luxury hotel lobby furniture package combines hammered brass display vitrines with green lacquered back-bar joinery, a marble-top service station and coordinating round tables. The photographs document workshop fabrication, dry-fit and lighting verification. They show the glazed displays before and during trial illumination, the assembled back bar, and the joints and finish interfaces of the individual pieces.

sections.title: Display Vitrines, Back-Bar Joinery and Coordinating Furniture
paragraphs: The display units pair textured brass frames and glazing with a lit drawer. The lobby package also includes lacquered tall cabinets, a back bar with brass shelf framing, and separate marble-topped pieces. The case records the fabricated units and how their materials and interfaces were reviewed in the workshop.

sections.title: Aligning Glazing, Hammered Brass and Lighting
paragraphs: Under the display light, the mitred brass corners and the line around the glazing remain visible at close range. The glazed drawer also introduces an extra perimeter where the fixed frame has to align with a moving part.

points.title: Hammered finish at the mitre
points.text: The change in plane at the corner creates a bright edge. Reviewing the joint close up shows whether the hammered surface and the visible frame meet cleanly on both faces.

points.title: Lit drawer and glazing
points.text: The open and closed drawer views make the fit between the glazed frame and lit display surface legible. Both positions matter when reviewing the appearance.

points.title: Back-bar material junctions
points.text: Brass framing crosses lacquered faces, shelving and stone worktop surfaces. The assembled view exposes where these lines meet and where cutouts interrupt the worktop.

sections.title: Vitrine Frames and Curved-End Cabinetry
paragraphs: The unlit workshop view makes the vitrine’s top frame, glazed sides and supporting legs easy to read. On the curved-end cabinet, the shelf ends and plinth share a rounded line, while the metal uprights continue past each shelf to form the taller assembly.

sections.title: Workshop Dry-Fit and Powered Display Check
paragraphs: The full-size vitrine appears with the drawer open and closed under warm trial lighting. The opening view reveals the illuminated display surface and the surrounding frame. The assembled back bar was also photographed as a complete workshop elevation with its worktop cutouts and shelf frame visible.

gallery.caption: The open drawer makes its illuminated display surface and its interface with the surrounding brass frame visible.

sections.title: Surface Finishes and Furniture Interfaces
paragraphs: Detail photographs record the texture across the mitred brass corner, the green lacquer meeting brass cabinet dividers, and the service station’s stone top and woven screen. The paired occasional tables show the relationship between the marble tops, their thin metal edges and the contrasting finishes of the turned bases.

gallery.caption: The close-up shows the 45-degree meeting of the brass faces at the glazed cabinet corner and the texture on either side of the joint.

gallery.caption: The straight-on workshop view reveals the alignment of the brass dividers with the green cabinet and its horizontal shelves.

gallery.caption: The service station brings a marble top, a woven metal screen and a two-door waste-sorting cabinet into the same brass framing system.

gallery.caption: A workshop view shows the circular tops, metal edge bands and two-tone turned bases of the coordinating tables.

sections.title: What to Specify for Hotel Vitrines and Lobby Joinery
paragraphs: The furniture schedule should show how the display, joinery and stone packages meet. Provide handling and building-services requirements alongside the finish details.

points.title: Drawings and schedules
points.text: Send CAD or PDF drawings identifying display clearances, drawer travel, glazing, joinery, worktop cutouts and the stone-to-metal interfaces.

points.title: Samples and powered views
points.text: Review a mitred hammered-brass sample, a lacquer sample and the specified stone together. Confirm the intended lighting tone and appearance with the drawer open and closed.

points.title: Access and servicing
points.text: Show service access for lighting, outlet and driver locations, the site delivery route and any piece-size limits for glazed units or stone tops.

conclusion: The workshop record shows the vitrine’s lighting and moving parts alongside the finish details of the assembled back bar and furniture. For a luxury hospitality package, submit CAD or PDF elevations, the material and equipment schedules, and the intended lighting so the interfaces and sample checks can be scoped from the same information.
